title: Signature precedence voting
description: A Signature method for settling requirement clashes: rank the colliding requirements by closeness to the user-stated goal, let the winner lead, and demote the loser to a constraint. Written as an original Signature technique.
signature_principle: The requirement closest to the user goal leads; the other becomes a constraint, never a second commander.
signature_method: Score each requirement 1-5 on user-goal proximity, reversibility cost, and blast radius; highest total wins.
signature_steps: List the colliding pair|Score each on the three axes|Declare the winner and demote the loser to a constraint|Record the decision with its scores in the contradiction ledger
signature_advantage: Decisions take minutes, stay explainable to stakeholders, and leave a paper trail.

title: Signature requirement shadowing
description: A Signature technique that keeps a losing requirement alive as a "shadow" — monitored, measured, but not blocking. If the shadow metric degrades, the decision is revisited automatically.
signature_principle: Losing requirements are not deleted; they are shadowed and watched.
signature_method: Attach the demoted requirement as a shadow metric with an alert threshold and a review date.
signature_steps: Demote the loser|Define its shadow metric and threshold|Wire the metric to the dashboard|Auto-schedule the revisit review
signature_advantage: No requirement dies silently; reversals happen on data, not politics.

title: Signature contradiction ledger
description: A Signature practice: every detected contradiction is logged with both requirements, the chosen resolution, and the signature of the decider. The ledger becomes the team memory of tradeoffs.
signature_principle: Every tradeoff is written down once, in one place, with a name attached.
signature_method: Append-only ledger entries: pair, type, severity, resolution, decider, date.
signature_steps: Detect the clash|Write the ledger entry|Link it from both requirement records|Review the ledger quarterly for patterns
signature_advantage: Recurring clash types get solved once and reused forever.

title: Signature dual-track acceptance
description: A Signature acceptance method: when requirements collide, ship both behaviors behind a per-tenant switch and let measured outcomes pick the winner within one quarter.
signature_principle: When analysis stalls, measurement decides — ship both, measure, keep the winner.
signature_method: Feature-flag both behaviors, define the deciding metric up front, and set a decision date.
signature_steps: Flag both behaviors|Define the deciding metric|Ship to a split cohort|Keep the winner on the decision date, delete the loser
signature_advantage: Ends religious debates with data; the losing code is deleted on schedule.

title: Signature severity auction
description: A Signature prioritization rite: stakeholders bid severity points on each side of a contradiction, forcing the real cost of each requirement into the open.
signature_principle: Severity is a budget, not an adjective — bidding reveals true priorities.
signature_method: Each stakeholder gets 10 severity points to distribute across the colliding requirements; totals set the priority.
signature_steps: Give each stakeholder 10 points|Collect blind bids|Publish the totals|Resolve in favor of the higher bid with the loser shadowed
signature_advantage: Exposes which requirement is truly load-bearing versus merely loud.

title: Signature stakeholder arbitration protocol
description: A Signature escalation path for contradictions that cross team boundaries: a 48-hour arbitration with written positions, a neutral decider, and a binding written ruling.
signature_principle: Cross-team clashes get a fast, written, binding ruling — never a hallway compromise.
signature_method: Written positions under one page, a decider with no stake, a ruling within 48 hours.
signature_steps: File written positions|Appoint a neutral decider|Hold a one-hour hearing|Publish the binding ruling to the ledger
signature_advantage: Stops contradiction ping-pong between teams; rulings compound into precedent.

title: Signature time-boxed exception
description: A Signature compromise pattern: grant the losing requirement a dated exception instead of a permanent defeat, so the clash resolves itself when the exception expires.
signature_principle: Temporary exceptions beat permanent arguments.
signature_method: Write the exception with an expiry date, an owner, and the condition that ends it early.
signature_steps: Define the exception scope|Set the expiry date and owner|Ship under the exception|Let expiry or the end-condition close it
signature_advantage: Unblocks shipping today while guaranteeing the debate ends on a date.

title: Signature scope slicing
description: A Signature decomposition move: split the contested scope so each requirement wins in its own slice — different user tiers, regions, or data classes obey different rules.
signature_principle: A contradiction is often two true statements about two different scopes.
signature_method: Find the scope axis (tier, region, data class, time) that lets both requirements hold somewhere.
signature_steps: Name the scope axis|Assign each requirement its slice|Draw the boundary in the spec|Test the boundary, not just each side
signature_advantage: Turns zero-sum fights into coexistence; boundaries are explicit and testable.

title: Signature constraint inversion
description: A Signature reframing: turn the blocking requirement into a design constraint that the winning requirement must satisfy, so "no" becomes "yes, if".
signature_principle: Every blocker is a constraint in disguise — invert it and design inside it.
signature_method: Rewrite the losing requirement as measurable constraints on the winning design.
signature_steps: State the blocker|Convert it to measurable constraints|Design the winner inside those constraints|Verify the constraints in CI
signature_advantage: Converts vetoes into engineering targets the team can actually hit.

title: Signature metric mediation
description: A Signature technique for non-functional clashes: translate both requirements into one shared metric and optimize that, so the argument becomes arithmetic.
signature_principle: If both sides can be measured on one scale, the scale decides.
signature_method: Define the shared metric, weight each side, and pick the design that maximizes it.
signature_steps: Define the shared metric|Weight each requirement|Score candidate designs|Ship the top scorer, ledger the math
signature_advantage: Replaces opinion with a number both sides agreed to beforehand.

description: A Signature UX method: build both conflicting experiences as throwaway prototypes and test with five users each before writing production code.

title: Signature risk transfer clause
description: A Signature contracting pattern: when a contradiction is forced by an external rule, write the residual risk into the contract so the accepting party owns it explicitly.
signature_principle: Forced tradeoffs are owned in writing, by name.
signature_method: Name the risk, quantify it, assign the owner, and countersign.
signature_steps: Name the residual risk|Quantify it plainly|Assign the owning party|Countersign and file with the requirement
signature_advantage: Nobody is surprised later; the tradeoff has an owner from day one.

title: Signature versioned requirement
description: A Signature spec discipline: when a requirement must contradict its past self, version it explicitly instead of editing history — v1 stays true for old data, v2 rules new data.
signature_principle: Requirements have versions like code; the past is never rewritten.
signature_method: Freeze the old requirement, publish the new one with a version, and define the migration boundary.
signature_steps: Freeze v1|Publish v2 with the change log|Define which data each version governs|Migrate across the boundary deliberately
signature_advantage: Ends "but the spec said" arguments; history stays auditable.
